blocks.text: Have you ever noticed how a fire warms up a room or how an ice pack cools down an injury? These are examples of exothermic and endothermic reactions.

blocks.markdown: In chemistry, reactions can either release energy or absorb energy. These reactions are classified as exothermic or endothermic, respectively. Understanding these types of reactions is crucial in fields such as energy production, environmental science, and even cooking.

blocks.title: Exothermic Reaction
blocks.text: An exothermic reaction is a chemical reaction that releases heat to its surroundings. Examples include combustion and respiration.

blocks.markdown: Exothermic reactions are characterized by a release of energy, usually in the form of heat. This means that the products have less energy than the reactants. In contrast, endothermic reactions absorb energy from their surroundings, resulting in products that have more energy than the reactants.

blocks.title: Endothermic Reaction
blocks.text: An endothermic reaction is a chemical reaction that absorbs heat from its surroundings. An example is the melting of ice.

blocks.title: Energy Profile Diagram for Exothermic Reaction
blocks.prompt: Sketch an energy profile diagram for an exothermic reaction and indicate the enthalpy change ($\Delta H$).

steps.text: Draw a graph with 'Energy' on the y-axis and 'Reaction Progress' on the x-axis.
Start with a high energy level for reactants and a lower energy level for products.
Draw a curve descending from the reactants to the products.
Mark the difference in energy as $\Delta H$, noting it is negative.

blocks.answer: The diagram should show a downward curve with $\Delta H$ labeled as negative, indicating energy release.

blocks.markdown: In an energy profile diagram for an exothermic reaction, the energy of the reactants is higher than that of the products, resulting in a negative $\Delta H$. This indicates that energy is released during the reaction.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Remember, in exothermic reactions, $\Delta H$ is negative because energy is released. In endothermic reactions, $\Delta H$ is positive because energy is absorbed.

points: Exothermic reactions release energy, resulting in products with lower energy than reactants.
Endothermic reactions absorb energy, resulting in products with higher energy than reactants.
In energy profile diagrams, $\Delta H$ is negative for exothermic reactions.
